title: Endpoints de IA, Hugging Face y prompting evaluado
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S25.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S21-S24 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED. S25 cannot treat OCR status=auto, S24 confidence>=0.85, S23 downloads, S22 approvals or S21 report values as trustworthy merely because earlier snippets emitted those labels.
usable: human review is distinct from model generation
score is not a legal/fraud verdict
untrusted external text must not become instructions
evidence should remain bound to source artifacts
not_creditable: S24 fields are fully provenance-bound or human-reviewed
S24 confidence is calibrated or even normalized consistently
S23 browser artifact is uniquely/currently verified
S22 approved state is bound to exact content and recipients

roadmap_expectation.T1: Selección: regla vs modelo especializado vs LLM; model cards, licencias y local/cloud
roadmap_expectation.T2: Inferencia: Hugging Face pipelines/endpoints; batching, timeout, cache, costo y fallback
roadmap_expectation.T3: Prompting: objetivo, contexto, restricciones, ejemplos y salida estructurada; GLM-5.2 thinking/tools/checkpoints
roadmap_expectation.T4: Evals/seguridad: golden set, schema y revisión humana; prompt injection, exfiltración, sesgo y minimización
roadmap_expectation.gate: clasificador/extractor especializado y generador de narrativa con JSON validado; no se acepta una salida sin evidencia ni eval contra baseline

live_site.evidence: Public page exposes Section 25 'IA endpoints y prompts' and the same baseline/evidence tagline. Hydrated theory body is not exposed by the public text surface, so render-only defects were not invented.

checks: deploy_choice returns cloud_or_local for the supplied card even though the same card lists fraud adjudication in not_for; the function itself never enforces intended/not_for.
T3-A canonical prompt does not contain PEN, yet the published output says 'Mediana Lima 28 PEN'.
T3-A output keys are hallazgo/n/mediana/limite, while the reference narrative contract requires hallazgo/n/mediana/evidence_ids/model.
schema_ok returns True for {'h':123,'n':'one'} because it validates key presence only.
field_match_rate({}, {'x': None}) returns 1.0; missing prediction is counted as correct when the gold value is null.
After three failures the simple circuit returns circuit=open even for a subsequent healthy-looking call; there is no half-open/recovery path.
injection_signal returns True for the canonical malicious document but build_request still constructs a model request carrying that same untrusted_document.
run_checkpointed marks an allowlisted tool ok=True without executing the tool or validating arguments/results.

external_research.source: Hugging Face Transformers current pipeline documentation
external_research.finding: TextClassificationPipeline returns label/score shapes and supports list inputs, but the model score is produced from model outputs; application adapters still need their own versioning/contract validation.

Cards should document model, intended uses, limitations/biases, training/datasets and evaluation; license is metadata, while out-of-scope uses are documented content rather than a universal structured not_for API field.
Endpoints have concrete auth/network/autoscaling/cost controls; current S25 deployment and ops mocks do not model endpoint identity, auth policy, revision, timeout client behavior or recovery state.

external_research.source: OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
external_research.finding: Untrusted content, output/action validation, least privilege and human approval are defense-in-depth controls; regex detection and textual delimiters are not sufficient.
GLM-5.2 is a current model with thinking/tool-relevant capabilities, so its complete omission from S25 theory is roadmap drift rather than an obsolete roadmap reference.

findings.evidence: Opening treats S24 extracted fields as available inputs for model judgment.
findings.attack: S24 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED: provenance, bbox lineage, monetary semantics, confidence normalization and review completion are not creditable.
findings.defense: Curriculum continuity requires consuming prior artifacts.
findings.impact: A model can amplify an upstream false-green field into a persuasive narrative/classification.
findings.repair: Require a validated S24 handoff record with source hash, raw+normalized values, confidence scale/version and review state; otherwise route human.

findings.evidence: All executable theory inference is a keyword mock or deterministic dict builder; real transformers/HTTP calls are comments/reference only.
findings.attack: Roadmap/title promise Hugging Face pipelines/endpoints and a classifier/extractor plus narrative generator.
findings.defense: Mocks make the lesson reproducible without downloading weights or requiring network access.
findings.impact: A learner can satisfy theory without demonstrating endpoint invocation, serialization, HTTP errors, provider auth or actual model output normalization.
findings.repair: Keep mocks, but add one controlled real/local transformers adapter or approved HTTP test double that exercises the same contract end-to-end.

findings.evidence: hf_mock is a keyword rule classifier and prompt_struct.build_output is a normal Python dict constructor; there is no specialized extractor and no model-generated narrative.
findings.attack: Tagline/gate claim specialized classifier/extractor and narrative generator.
findings.defense: The lesson intentionally focuses on contracts rather than weights.
findings.impact: The most important nouns in the gate are simulated away, so model-specific failure modes never appear.
findings.repair: Demonstrate at least one actual specialized model output and one model-generated structured narrative on synthetic data, both behind deterministic contract tests.

findings.evidence: choose_stack hardcodes specialized_model when n_train >= 500.
findings.attack: No universal 500-example threshold determines whether a specialized model is appropriate; task difficulty, class balance, label quality, baseline and model family matter.
findings.defense: A simple threshold reduces novice decision complexity.
findings.impact: Learner can treat sample count as scientific selection criterion instead of a toy lab heuristic.
findings.repair: Label 500 explicitly as a fixture value and make measured validation vs baseline the actual selection gate.

findings.evidence: choose_stack selects rules/specialized/LLM from task flags before any quality, latency, privacy, cost or baseline measurement.
findings.attack: The section's own promotion contract requires eval vs baseline, yet stack selection is rule-of-thumb only.
findings.defense: T4 evaluates later.
findings.impact: Architecture can be locked in before evidence shows it adds value.
findings.repair: Use the tree only to generate candidates; final choice must compare candidates on the same fixed eval set plus operational/governance constraints.

findings.evidence: Prose/code treat card['not_for'] as though it were a universal structured model-card field.
findings.attack: Hugging Face model cards are Markdown+metadata; out-of-scope/misuse information is documented content and not guaranteed as a normalized not_for key.
findings.defense: The lab can normalize documentation into a local governance record.
findings.impact: Learner may expect machine-readable fields that many real cards do not provide.
findings.repair: State that not_for is the course's normalized governance field extracted from Out-of-Scope Use/limitations, and preserve source evidence.

findings.evidence: deploy_choice only checks has_pii_live and a two-license allowlist; intended/not_for is explicitly delegated to the caller.
findings.attack: The same prohibited-use card can return cloud_or_local; policy safety depends on another caller remembering an unstated composition order.
findings.defense: The comment says the caller applies blocked_use separately.
findings.impact: A governance check can be skipped while deployment still returns a positive choice.
findings.repair: Create one fail-closed deployment policy that combines intended/out-of-scope use, license/legal review, data class, provider approval, residency/retention and network/auth controls.

findings.evidence: Prose promises model/card version metadata; executable adapters emit only model='demo-cls' or model='demo' and no revision/card hash/config.
findings.attack: A mutable model id cannot reproduce a past classification or cache entry.
findings.defense: Synthetic fixture ids are stable within one code sample.
findings.impact: Golden results and cached outputs cannot be bound to exact model artifacts/configuration.
findings.repair: Persist model repository/id + immutable revision/hash, task/config, tokenizer/prompt/schema versions and card source hash.

findings.evidence: Classifier contract checks are described as keys/types, but hf_mock simply returns dicts; no validator enforces label enum, score numeric/range, cardinality or model revision.
findings.attack: Same shape does not guarantee semantically compatible adapters.
findings.defense: The mock illustrates the base label/score shape documented by HF.
findings.impact: An endpoint with malformed score/unknown label can pass downstream until later logic breaks.
findings.repair: Implement an explicit adapter validator for list cardinality, types, label domain, finite score range and immutable model metadata.

findings.evidence: T2-A says injection indications go human_review, but classifier adapter accepts arbitrary texts without a trust marker or injection/risk route.
findings.attack: S24 OCR is explicitly untrusted_document_content from the carry-forward contract.
findings.defense: Detailed injection controls appear in T4-B.
findings.impact: The primary inference path can consume document directives before the promised security gate is demonstrated.
findings.repair: Carry trust/source metadata through every adapter and centralize the policy route before any model/tool-capable path.

findings.evidence: Outcome promises batching and timeout operation; code loops a list in a mock and simulates timeout with fail=True rather than configuring a client/request timeout or batch policy.
findings.attack: Operational behavior is asserted but not exercised.
findings.defense: Network-independent simulation is deliberate.
findings.impact: Learner does not practice batch sizing, provider response cardinality, timeout configuration or client-specific timeout exceptions.
findings.repair: Add controlled batch and HTTP-client test-double cases for partial/malformed batch responses and configured timeout exceptions.

findings.evidence: cache key is sha256(model|text)[:12].
findings.attack: It omits immutable model revision, task/config, prompt/schema/tokenizer version and policy; truncation also weakens collision margin.
findings.defense: For a tiny synthetic pure classifier, model+text often determines output.
findings.impact: A model/config update can reuse stale output as if current.
findings.repair: Hash the complete canonical inference identity with full SHA-256; use a short prefix only for display.

findings.evidence: cost=COST_PER_1K*len(text)/1000 while prose says tokens or requests; no currency/provider/pricing version is recorded.
findings.attack: Characters are not tokens and per-request pricing is a different unit.
findings.defense: It is a toy estimate.
findings.impact: Learner may treat an arbitrary character formula as a cloud cost estimate.
findings.repair: Declare the unit explicitly; for token pricing use the actual tokenizer/usage response, and version provider/model/currency/pricing date.

findings.evidence: One global failures counter opens after 3 and never transitions half-open/closed; no timer, endpoint key or alert is implemented.
findings.attack: Runtime probe shows even a later healthy-looking call returns circuit=open forever.
findings.defense: The heading explicitly says circuit breaker simple.
findings.impact: One endpoint/model can permanently disable all inference in-process and there is no recovery probe or observable alert.
findings.repair: Scope breaker by dependency, add closed/open/half_open state with cooldown/recovery probe and emit an alert/event when state changes.

findings.evidence: Open circuit returns {'fallback':'rules_or_human'} but executes neither a rule nor a human-review enqueue.
findings.attack: A label is not a fallback path.
findings.defense: The example is intended to teach routing semantics.
findings.impact: Downstream code can mistake a routing hint for handled work.
findings.repair: Return a typed routing decision consumed by an actual deterministic fallback or persisted review item; never present it as completed inference.

findings.evidence: Reference contract requires hallazgo,n,mediana,evidence_ids,model; T3-A outputs hallazgo,n,mediana,limite.
findings.attack: The canonical prompting example omits both evidence linkage and model identity.
findings.defense: limite demonstrates a useful limitation field.
findings.impact: An output can satisfy the displayed prompt while violating the section's authoritative narrative contract and tagline evidence requirement.
findings.repair: Use one versioned narrative schema everywhere; include evidence_ids/model and optional limitations as an additional validated field.

findings.evidence: PROMPT context contains 'mediana Lima=28 n=40' but generated example says 'Mediana Lima 28 PEN'.
findings.attack: PEN is absent from the supplied context, directly violating 'no inventes'.
findings.defense: Earlier reporting sections often use PEN.
findings.impact: The canonical example normalizes exactly the unsupported factual addition the section says to reject.
findings.repair: Include unit=PEN in the trusted context/evidence or remove PEN from hallazgo; add a grounding validator against supplied fields.

findings.evidence: Narrative fixture uses mediana=28.0 and hallazgo='28 PEN'.
findings.attack: S02 established Decimal/integer-cent semantics for money; S24 monetary float was explicitly not creditable.
findings.defense: This is display-only synthetic data.
findings.impact: The AI layer reintroduces floating-point monetary semantics into evidence/reporting.
findings.repair: Pass canonical monetary values as Decimal/string minor-unit representations and format for display separately.

findings.evidence: schema_ok and T3-A validation require key presence only; runtime accepts {'h':123,'n':'one'}.
findings.attack: The gate says JSON validado and the contracts specify typed semantic fields.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly calls this a minimum gate rather than full JSON Schema.
findings.impact: Type-invalid, out-of-domain or unexpected-property output can be called schema-valid.
findings.repair: Keep the key-presence exercise as first layer, then validate types, enums/ranges, required evidence ids and additional-properties policy with a real schema validator or equivalent code.

findings.evidence: No code verifies hallazgo/n/mediana against trusted S24/S21 values or checks that evidence_ids exist.
findings.attack: S25 repeatedly promises no output without evidence, but structural JSON alone does not prove grounding.
findings.defense: T4 prose says evidence_ids should exist in the OCR fixture.
findings.impact: A fluent but fabricated value/reference can pass schema validation and golden plumbing.
findings.repair: Validate every evidence id against the run's evidence registry and compare derived numeric claims to canonical values/units before human review.

findings.evidence: Roadmap T3 explicitly names GLM-5.2 thinking/tools/checkpoints; canonical S25 deliberately removes product-specific treatment and never mentions GLM-5.2.
findings.attack: GLM-5.2 is current, so the omission is not justified by obsolescence.
findings.defense: Generic patterns transfer better across providers.
findings.impact: Roadmap promises a concrete model-specific capability that learners never see, while source silently changes scope.
findings.repair: Either revise roadmap to generic provider-neutral reasoning/tools or add a clearly optional GLM-5.2 mapping that remains subordinate to generic safety contracts.

findings.evidence: run_checkpointed logs {'think': note} as an auditable checkpoint.
findings.attack: Hidden chain-of-thought is not a portable API contract and logging private reasoning is unnecessary; auditable systems should log plans, decisions, tool intents/results and policy reasons.
findings.defense: The fixture uses an explicit synthetic note, not an actual provider chain-of-thought.
findings.impact: Learner may build observability around unavailable/sensitive reasoning text instead of externally verifiable actions.
findings.repair: Rename to plan/rationale summary and never require or persist hidden chain-of-thought.

findings.evidence: Tool policy checks only step['name']; arguments, resource scope, side-effect class and original user intent are absent, and allowed tools are logged ok=True without execution.
findings.attack: Allowlisted function names can still perform unsafe actions with malicious arguments.
findings.defense: The lab focuses on the first allowlist concept.
findings.impact: The learner can mistake name allowlisting for least privilege/action authorization.
findings.repair: Validate tool name + typed args + resource/tenant + side-effect policy + approval requirement, execute through a sandboxed adapter, then validate result.

findings.evidence: Prose promises plan→tool→validar→narrar; code implements think/tool/deny only and hardcodes ok=True.
findings.attack: No validation or narration checkpoint exists.
findings.defense: It demonstrates stop-on-denial.
findings.impact: Successful tool status is fabricated and the highest-risk boundary—validating tool output before narration—is absent.
findings.repair: Model explicit plan, authorization, execution, result validation and narrative stages with typed statuses/evidence.

findings.evidence: field_match_rate uses pred.get(k)==gold.get(k) across union keys.
findings.attack: Runtime: field_match_rate({}, {'x':None}) == 1.0, so a missing prediction is counted correct when gold is null.
findings.defense: Using union avoids KeyError for missing keys.
findings.impact: Field accuracy can be inflated by absence rather than correct prediction.
findings.repair: Compare key presence separately from value equality; a missing key must be a miss unless the schema explicitly defines omission as the gold representation.

findings.evidence: eval_rows divides by len(rows) with no empty-set contract.
findings.attack: eval_rows([]) raises ZeroDivisionError.
findings.defense: The shown fixture is nonempty.
findings.impact: A filtered/no-eligible slice crashes instead of reporting not_evaluable and n=0.
findings.repair: Return a typed not_evaluable result with n, denominators and exclusion reasons.

findings.evidence: T4-A code evaluates only model predictions; no baseline rows, model revision, fixed eval-set id or promotion rule are present.
findings.attack: Tagline/callout explicitly say no acceptance without eval vs baseline, and the figure says cases must not change between rounds.
findings.defense: The prose names rules/model anterior as baseline.
findings.impact: There is no executable evidence that the AI improves over a simpler alternative or that prompt iterations use the same test set.
findings.repair: Evaluate candidate and baseline on the identical versioned golden set, persist metrics/cost/latency/safety, and define a fail-closed promotion rule.

findings.evidence: human_review/HITL appears as strings/booleans; no persisted review item, reviewer, timestamp, decision or corrected output exists.
findings.attack: A routing label does not demonstrate human review.
findings.defense: S26 later orchestrates HITL more fully.
findings.impact: S25 can claim outputs are reviewed without evidence a human ever saw them.
findings.repair: At minimum emit a review record schema and require an explicit reviewed decision before downstream report/email use.

findings.evidence: injection_signal(doc) is True for the canonical malicious document, but build_request(doc) is still called and contains the same untrusted document.
findings.attack: The section rule says injection indications derive to human_review.
findings.defense: The text correctly says regex is telemetry, not the real control.
findings.impact: The executable example demonstrates detection without enforcement and can normalize 'flagged but still sent' behavior.
findings.repair: Make policy routing explicit: signal may raise review/deny, while defense-in-depth still treats undetected content as untrusted and constrains outputs/actions.

findings.evidence: build_request sets requires_human_approval=True but no controller consumes it; system/untrusted_document are custom dict fields rather than a demonstrated provider role/action boundary.
findings.attack: A boolean declaration does not block an external action.
findings.defense: The request object is a policy contract rather than a send action.
findings.impact: Learner can confuse metadata with enforcement.
findings.repair: Separate generation from action execution and enforce approval in the action gateway using a persisted reviewer decision bound to exact output/action.

findings.evidence: T4-B says route policy auto_fraud_label=False, but no theory code actually carries or asserts that field.
findings.attack: A stated policy has no executable regression guard.
findings.defense: Other prose repeatedly says score is not fraud.
findings.impact: Future adapters can regress to an autonomous sensitive label without failing the shown tests.
findings.repair: Make prohibited downstream decisions an explicit contract/test and verify no adapter maps model score to fraud adjudication.

findings.evidence: Dense terms include stack, fine-tuned, label set, golden, baseline, adapter, batch, cache, fallback, circuit breaker, schema rate, prompt injection, tools/checkpoints/HITL.
findings.attack: Many are introduced in clusters rather than Spanish-first causal explanations.
findings.defense: Several terms receive parenthetical translations.
findings.impact: High code-switching load competes with already difficult model-risk concepts.
findings.repair: Introduce Spanish concept first, keep API literals in code, and repeat one stable term thereafter.

findings.evidence: S25-eval-loop sits under T2-A Pipelines/endpoints, but caption/alt describe prompt→output→evaluate→adjust and fixed evaluation cases.
findings.attack: The figure visually teaches T3/T4 prompt evaluation while learner is studying adapter normalization.
findings.defense: Evaluation continuity is relevant to any adapter.
findings.impact: The scarce diagram creates split attention instead of dual-coding the current endpoint contract.
findings.repair: Move eval-loop to T4-A; give T2-A a diagram raw HF/HTTP response→adapter normalization→contract validation→typed result/human_review.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: HF text-classification pipeline does not return label/score.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Current Transformers documentation shows [{'label':..., 'score':...}] for text classification; the defect is the missing application adapter validation/versioning, not the base HF shape.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Regex injection detection is presented as sufficient security.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The prose explicitly calls regex telemetry rather than a real control. The confirmed defect is that the executable policy detects the malicious fixture yet still constructs the model request.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Using mock models is inherently pedagogically wrong.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Mocks are appropriate for deterministic contract tests; the defect is that the section gate/title claims real endpoint/model capabilities without any executed bridge to one real adapter.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Cloud endpoints can never process personal data.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: That is not a universal technical fact. S25's no-real-PII-to-public-endpoints rule is a conservative course policy; the problem is incomplete executable deployment governance, not the conservative boundary itself.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: A model score is always a calibrated probability.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: S25 does not call score a legal probability and repeatedly says score is only a signal. No false claim was charged here.

source_only.text: Read `title` below, never the slug. Matching content to the slug is how three agent diagrams ended up attached to a data-testing lesson.

usable: untrusted document text is data, not authority
score is not a fraud/legal verdict
tools are privileges and denial should stop execution
human review is required for uncertain/high-risk outputs
misconception_risk: 500 examples is a universal specialized-model threshold
not_for is a universal machine-readable model-card key
model id without revision is enough provenance
model+text short hash is sufficient cache identity
open circuit without recovery is a complete breaker
key presence means JSON contract valid
injection detected but still sent is acceptable
allowlisted tool name alone authorizes a tool call

priority_order: F16/F17/F19/F20: make the canonical narrative contract grounded, typed and evidence-bound; remove the published hallucination.
F27/F25/F26: implement honest fixed-set baseline evaluation and correct field/denominator semantics.
F29/F30/F23/F24: turn security/tool/approval declarations into enforced policy boundaries.
F02/F03: add a real controlled adapter/model bridge so the gate measures AI endpoints rather than mocks alone.
F12/F14/F15/F11/F13: repair operational inference identity, cache, circuit, fallback, timeout/batch and cost semantics.
F01/F08/F18: preserve upstream provenance and monetary/model revision semantics.
F04/F05/F06/F07/F09/F10/F21/F22/F31/F32/F33: tighten selection/governance, roadmap alignment, terminology and visual pedagogy.
